entries.title: Palestinians told to leave homes in village where Israeli settlers besieged houses
entries.snippet: The mayor of Qusra says Israeli troops have been telling families to leave their houses, using some as barracks.

entries.title: Romania shuts only nuclear plant as heat causes huge drop in Danube River level
entries.snippet: The Cernavodă plant, which produces 20% of Romania's electricity, is not expected to be restarted within the next 10 days.

entries.title: Putin can no longer claim victory in Ukraine, Nobel Peace Prize winner tells BBC
entries.snippet: In an exclusive interview with the BBC’s Steve Rosenberg, Dmitry Muratov says the Kremlin leader can only "destroy Ukraine, not conquer it", with the war now in its fifth year.

entries.title: Engine parts smashed Ryanair window that man's head was sucked out of, report says
entries.snippet: A preliminary report by US investigators says an engine fan blade broke on last month's flight from Greece to Germany.

entries.title: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms
entries.snippet: Thousands of sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

entries.title: Person fined after using foghorn to wake sleeping polar bear
entries.snippet: Under local regulations in the region, "it is forbidden to needlessly disturb, attract or pursue a polar bear".

entries.title: Mangione lawyers to meet federal prosecutors amid reports of plea deal
entries.snippet: Mangione faces two federal charges of stalking resulting in death, each carrying a maximum sentence of life in prison.

entries.title: Family of Irish plane crash victim awarded $29m in damages
entries.snippet: A jury in Chicago in the US awarded the sum to Michael Ryan's family after his widow Naoise Connolly Ryan brought a civil suit against Boeing.

entries.title: Air India to test all pilots for banned substances
entries.snippet: It comes after one of its planes suddenly lost altitude last week, with a number of passengers injured.

entries.title: Four Canadian hockey stars remain suspended after sexual assault acquittal
entries.snippet: A fifth has been reinstated, though an appeals board found that the whole group broke Hockey Canada's code of conduct.

entries.title: Eurovision Song Contest 2027 to be held in Burgas, Bulgaria
entries.snippet: The Black Sea location has been selected after Bulgarian singer Dara won this year's contest.

entries.title: Presidential pardon for French alleged spy accused of plotting Mali coup
entries.snippet: France is yet to comment on Yann Vezilier's pardon and previously called the accusations "unfounded".

entries.title: Travis Kelce shares first details from his wedding to Taylor Swift: 'Best night of my life'
entries.snippet: In the comments, Kelce called Swift his "wife" for first time and said it was a "childhood dream" to wed at Madison Square Garden.

entries.title: French ambassador to CAR accused of misconduct at official residence faces disciplinary action
entries.snippet: The accusations against Bruno Foucher prompted investigations into a potential security breach.

entries.title: Indian actor's video with endangered gibbon sparks investigation
entries.snippet: A deleted video of Tamil star Vikram cuddling an endangered gibbon has triggered an inquiry into how the animal entered India.

entries.title: Three men will be executed on the same day as death penalties rise in US
entries.snippet: Despite growing opposition to the death penalty, one state is behind the rising numbers.

entries.title: Japan PM says Putin's visit to disputed islands 'absolutely unacceptable'
entries.snippet: It was the first time the Russian leader had visited the Kuril islands, according to state media.

entries.title: Australian army whistleblower released on parole after more than two years in jail
entries.snippet: David McBride was jailed after pleading guilty to leaking military secrets about Afghanistan.

entries.title: Thousands of Canadians call for US ambassador's expulsion
entries.snippet: An online petition accusing Pete Hoekstra of diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs has garnered more than 60,000 signatures.

entries.title: Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
entries.snippet: Grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine are falling as both countries attack each other's shipping facilities and ports.

entries.title: Kennedy Center Board votes again to shut main building down — and add Trump's name back
entries.snippet: The board voted to close the Washington, D.C., arts complex's main campus for a $250 million renovation — three months after a federal judge temporarily blocked a similar closure.

entries.title: Mangione could plead guilty in federal case ahead of N.Y. murder trial
entries.snippet: A surprise hearing this Friday in federal court has added to speculation that Luigi Mangione could enter a plea, which could derail a state murder trial.

entries.title: Vladimir Putin's first visit to disputed Pacific islands draws Tokyo protest
entries.snippet: The four southernmost islands of the chain also are claimed by Japan, which calls them the Northern Territories.

entries.title: By sky and sea, Ukraine's drone strikes challenge Russia's grip on Crimea
entries.snippet: Russia maintained an iron grip on Crimea since seizing it from Ukraine in 2014. Many Russian civilians go there to enjoy the beaches. But now Ukraine is hitting Crimea hard, upending daily life.

entries.title: Taiwan briefly slows its mobile internet to text-only speed as part of defense drill
entries.snippet: The drills come amid rising tensions with China, which frequently sends military planes and ships towards Taiwan.

entries.title: Inflation eased slightly in July. And, ICE plans to give officers electric shock gloves
entries.snippet: Inflation cooled a bit last month, according to a new report from the Labor Department. And, ICE plans to equip its officers with electric shock gloves.

entries.title: The drug lenacapavir is a mighty weapon against HIV. Its rollout gets mixed reviews
entries.snippet: It's a twice-a-year injection that is remarkably effective in preventing an HIV infection. Distribution is starting. But questions are being raised about getting it to the areas that need it most.

entries.title: Primary voters send mixed signals about what they want from the Democratic Party
entries.snippet: Primary results this month in Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin paint a muddled picture of just how far to the left Democratic voters want their candidates to be come this fall's midterm elections.

entries.title: U.S. ambassador calls settler siege of Palestinian homes a 'horrific act of terror'
entries.snippet: The U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemned the actions of Jewish settlers who are besieging the home of an American Palestinian family in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

entries.title: Sailors and their families have lives on hold, uncertain if they'll return to Mideast
entries.snippet: Sailors and family members who were evacuated from U.S. bases in the Middle East months ago are waiting for the military to figure out what will happen to the lives they left behind.

entries.title: Judge drops Nevada case against electors accused of forging 2020 election certificate
entries.snippet: The dismissal marks the latest setback in swing states' efforts to prosecute fake electors who tried to keep Trump in the White House after he lost to Joe Biden in 2020.

entries.title: The 71st Eurovision contest will take place in Bulgaria's Black Sea city of Burgas
entries.snippet: Next year's Eurovision Song Contest will take place in Burgas, a port city on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, organizers said Thursday.

entries.title: Trump administration ends funding for Arctic climate report
entries.snippet: The Trump administration said it would stop funding the Arctic Report Card, the longstanding effort to collect research on how the fastest-warming place on Earth is changing. It's the latest in a series of moves by the administration to curtail scientific research into the impact

entries.title: Baby elephant at National Zoo helps lead fight against deadly disease
entries.snippet: Elephant endotheliotropic herpesvirus is the leading cause of death in young Asian elephants. One baby elephant is at the center of an effort that could transform how the disease is managed in these gentle giants worldwide. Deema Zein reports.

entries.title: Teacher empowers her students to see themselves as art
entries.snippet: An artist and educator in Washington, D.C., is using her work to celebrate her students while confronting the lasting effects of redlining. Blu Murphy is helping young people see themselves and their communities as works of art. Shane Mukasa of our journalism training program, PB

entries.title: Jury selected for trial of former gang leader accused of ordering Tupac Shakur's fatal shooting
entries.snippet: Opening statements at the murder trial in Las Vegas are expected to begin Monday.

entries.title: Taliban detained 6 staff from a women's and children's rights group, Human Rights Watch says
entries.snippet: The six men — employees of the Women and Children Legal Research Foundation — were detained on July 18 after they were told to come to their office to retrieve confiscated laptops and phones, Human Rights Watch said in a statement released late Wednesday.

entries.title: Ukrainian drones strike major oil refinery deep inside Russia, setting it ablaze
entries.snippet: Russia is one of the world's biggest energy producers, with oil providing an economic mainstay as its military tries to push deeper into Ukraine in a slow and costly advance more than four years after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion.

entries.title: AP report: Luigi Mangione expected to plead guilty in federal case over CEO killing
entries.snippet: Luigi Mangione is expected to plead guilty as early as Friday in the federal case accusing him of stalking and killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, a person familiar with the matter told The Associated Press.

entries.title: Judge dismisses Trump administration lawsuit alleging antisemitism at Harvard
entries.snippet: The decision from U.S. District Judge Richard G. Stearns said President Donald Trump's administration failed to prove an ongoing violation of federal civil rights laws.

entries.title: Kennedy Center board moves forward with a two-year closure to allow for renovations
entries.snippet: The Kennedy Center will move forward with a two-year closure of the sprawling performing arts venue to allow for substantial renovation work, while some outdoor programming may continue.

entries.title: UK records hottest day of the year as western Europe swelters once again
entries.snippet: Britain, like France, is experiencing its fifth heat wave of the year, with the first recorded in May.

entries.title: Trump White House says it's losing $19B-$26 billion a year in revenue as countries dodge tariffs
entries.snippet: The report specifically highlights that China responded to new tariffs in 2018 by sending their goods to other nations ranging from Mexico to Malaysia for packaging and limited assembly — a practice known as transshipping.

entries.title: Zambians cast ballots in a presidential election that tests incumbent's economic reforms
entries.snippet: About 8 million people in the southern African country of 22 million were registered to vote in the one-day election. Voters also were choosing members of Parliament and local government councilors.

entries.title: Romania begins shutdown of nuclear plant's 2nd reactor amid low water levels on Danube River
entries.snippet: Scorching heat and low rainfall in recent weeks have left the Danube River at record lows and forced the state-owned Cernavoda plant to shut down its first reactor in late July.

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Kennedy Center board approves Trump name on facade, renovation plan
entries.snippet: The move appears designed to circumvent a judge's ruling that the US president's name should be removed, potentially setting the stage for a new legal fight over the Kennedy Center's name and future.

entries.title: US disputes reports of trying conditions on carrier in Gulf
entries.snippet: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called reports of poor conditions and mental health strain aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Middle East "completely misrepresented." Senators want an investigation.

entries.title: When the earth moves: six major earthquakes of 2026
entries.snippet: Colombia, Venezuela, Mindanao: Thousands have died in powerful earthquakes this year. Six such events show that the magnitude of the quake is not the only factor determining the scale of the disaster.

entries.title: Israeli military moves as settlers besiege 3 West Bank homes
entries.snippet: Israel's military has moved to try to stop a group of settlers from besieging three homes in the occupied West Bank. One was owned by a Palestinian American, prompting an unusually sharp rebuke from the US ambassador.

entries.title: Ukraine's monthly civilian casualties highest since 2022
entries.snippet: UN monitors say civilian casualties in Ukraine hit their highest monthly level since the start of Russia's full-scale war. The latest attacks included a Russian drone strike on a train, killing two workers.

entries.title: How Germany's drone defense fails
entries.snippet: Drone defense is a priority for the German government. The latest dramatic incident involving an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport shows there are still substantial shortcomings.

entries.title: Eritrea: a rising power along a global shipping artery
entries.snippet: Amid growing tensions and security risks in the Horn of Africa, Eritrea, with its strategically important coastal points on the Red Sea, is emerging as an important player in the region.

entries.title: What would a North Korean troop surge mean for Ukraine war?
entries.snippet: Ukraine is claiming that North Korea is preparing to send tens of thousands more troops to Russia, where they'll gain valuable battlefield experience.

entries.title: Germany: Buildings evacuated over suspected explosive
entries.snippet: Rail traffic was suspended in a region of Bavaria and authorities evacuated buildings around a train station after a suspicious object was found on the tracks. Police later confirmed it did not contain explosives.

entries.title: Germany news: Far-right leader backs left-wing populist
entries.snippet: The leader of the far-right AfD in Thuringia, Björn Höcke, has offered to back populist Sahra Wagenknecht as state premier. And heat-related deaths this year are now numbered at some 12,500. DW has more.

entries.title: India news: Parliament ends turbulent monsoon session
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was present as the session marked by a fierce standoff over student protests wrapped up.

entries.title: Colombia earthquake: Rescue operation enters 'final phase'
entries.snippet: Rescuers are racing against a critical 72-hour window to find survivors after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake that has killed 265 people, left hundreds missing, and displaced tens of thousands across western Colombia.

entries.title: US: Karoline Leavitt to step down as Trump's spokesperson
entries.snippet: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt is to leave her job at the end of the month, President Donald Trump says. Leavitt, 28, is the youngest-ever person to have held the position.

entries.title: Does the clean energy transition need forever chemicals?
entries.snippet: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?

entries.title: Russia's Putin angers Japan with 1st visit to Kuril Islands
entries.snippet: Japan says it has summoned the Russian ambassador to "strongly protest" President Vladimir Putin's trip to the disputed Kuril Islands.

entries.title: How North Korea has profited from its support for Russia
entries.snippet: Exceptionally high revenues, particularly from war aid for Russia, are consolidating the power of North Korea's autocratic leader. A small number of people in the country are benefiting from an economic boom.

entries.title: Brazil orders Discord to halt livestreaming after teen death
entries.snippet: Brazil has ordered Discord to suspend livestreaming as authorities scrutinize how the platform protects young users. The move follows a case described a "real-life horror show" that has triggered national outrage.

entries.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
entries.snippet: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

entries.title: Why is Russia's Yabloko party barred from upcoming election?
entries.snippet: Russia's highest court has banned anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary election. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in the country?
